About this map

Solving 9-11: people, positions and claimed connections

This map charts everyone and everything named in Christopher Bollyn's Solving 9-11: The Deception That Changed the World (2009–10 edition, foreword plus 14 chapters): 236 people and 89 organizations or events, grouped into 20 hubs around the book's thesis. Two further hubs add 30 entries from Bollyn's other writing (2005–2018 articles) that are not in this edition. These circles have a dotted halo. Dov Zakheim and Paul Wolfowitz appear there only through PNAC's 2000 report, which Bollyn quotes. In all there are 276 labelled relationships and 170 sources. Book text on archive.org.

Reader's note. This is a map of what the book asserts. Titles and positions are stated as fact; each connection and description is the book's claim, reported as such. Being on the map does not mean a person had any role in the September 11 attacks. The 9/11 Commission attributed the attacks to al-Qaeda hijackers, and NIST attributed the collapses of WTC 1, 2 and 7 to impact damage and fire. The book rejects those findings. Its central thesis, that Israeli intelligence planned the attacks, is not supported by those investigations and has been widely criticized, including as antisemitic. The map does not repeat the book's ethnic and religious labels for individuals; notes marked “outside the book” add facts that materially qualify a claim.

Using it. Scroll or pinch to zoom, and drag to pan. Click a circle for details, connections and source links (original URL, Wayback Machine copy, web search). Click a dark hub to fit that theme. Cross-links shows every tie between hubs. The coloured chips filter by role, and the number badge on a circle counts its links into other hubs. The companion PDF has the same maps as printable pages, plus a directory and source index.
